subject.title: refactor(infra): move exec approvals into the shared SQLite state DB

question: Should this release intentionally require existing exec-approval users to run `openclaw doctor --fix` before any approval-dependent execution resumes, instead of retaining a runtime compatibility reader?
rationale: The repository policy favors Doctor-owned migration and canonical runtime state, but this change deliberately converts a stored authorization policy into a fail-closed operator action during upgrade; that availability-versus-boundary decision requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Confirm the Doctor-gated cutover
options.body: Accept the no-runtime-compatibility design, with explicit operator and release guidance that existing approval state must be migrated before execution resumes.

options.title: Pause for release-path confirmation
options.body: Keep the PR open until the release owner confirms the intended upgrade communication and recovery expectations for users whose commands become unavailable.

recommendation.title: Confirm the Doctor-gated cutover
recommendation.body: Accept the no-runtime-compatibility design, with explicit operator and release guidance that existing approval state must be migrated before execution resumes.

likelyOwner.reason: The available commit history and the related merged repair show direct ownership of the exec-approvals persistence and migration direction.
